extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent owners, patent practitioners, and third‑party requesters involved in patent reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards for conducting ex parte and inter partes patent reexamination proceedings at the USPTO, including amendment format, filing requirements, assignment, tracking, and decision criteria under 35 U.S.C. 302–304 and relevant CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and entity reductions for reexamination petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petitions relating to a reexamination proceeding require fees (37 CFR 1.17(m) and 1.20(c)(6)). Micro entity reductions are available to patent owners only. Small entity and micro entity reductions are available to the patent owner for excess claim fees, appeal, appeal forwarding, and oral hearing fees. For the request and petition fees, small entity reductions are available to both third party requesters and patent owners; however, micro entity reductions are available only to patent owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a fee is required in a merged proceeding, only a single fee is needed even though multiple copies of submissions (one for each file) are required. Amendments that comply with the cited CFR provisions and contain required fees will be entered in the reexamination file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing/transmittal of Office actions to requester
rubrics_metrics.description: A transmittal form with the requester’s address will be used to forward copies of Office actions (and any references cited in the Office actions) to the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever an Office action is issued, a copy of the transmittal form will be made and attached to a copy of the Office action. The use of this form removes the need to retype the requester’s address each time a mailing is required. When the patent owner is the requester, no such form is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of making amendments (statutory/regulatory basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amendment to the description and claims in patents involved in reexamination proceedings must be made in accordance with 37 CFR 1.530.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment paper directing specified changes must be filed; it may accompany an owner request under 1.510(e), be part of a patent owner statement under paragraph (b), or be submitted during prosecution where permitted (e.g., §1.550(a), §1.937). Formal requirements for papers are set out in §1.52.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendments format
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification, other than to the claims, must be made by submission of the entire text of an added or rewritten paragraph including markings pursuant to paragraph (f) of this section, except that an entire paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting the paragraph, without presentation of the text of the paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The precise point in the specification must be identified where any added or rewritten paragraph is located. This applies whether the amendment is submitted on paper or compact disc (see §§1.96 and 1.825).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims amendment format
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment paper must include the entire text of each patent claim which is being proposed to be changed by such amendment paper and of each new claim being proposed to be added by such amendment paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For any claim changed, a parenthetical expression (“amended,” “twice amended,” etc.) should follow the claim number. Each changed or added claim must include markings pursuant to paragraph (f), except that a claim may be canceled by a statement canceling the claim without presentation of the text of the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendment format and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to the patent drawings must be submitted as a sketch on a separate paper showing the proposed changes in red for approval by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon examiner approval, new sheets including the changes and in compliance with §1.84 must be filed. Amended figures must be identified as “Amended,” any added figure identified as “New,” and canceled figures surrounded by brackets and identified as “Canceled.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal presentation requirement for amendments (full text)
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments in reexamination proceedings must be presented in the form of a full copy of the text of each claim which is amended and each paragraph of the description which is amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In other words, the entire claim or paragraph must be presented for any amendment. If a portion of the text is amended more than once, each amendment should indicate ALL of the changes (insertions and deletions) in relation to the current text of the patent under reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of claims and support for claim changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there is an amendment to the claims pursuant to paragraph (d), there must also be supplied, on pages separate from the pages containing the changes, the status (i.e., pending or canceled), as of the date of the amendment, of all patent claims and of all added claims, and an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent for the changes to the claims made by the amendment paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The support explanation should demonstrate where in the disclosure the changes are supported; this is required separate from the amended claim text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings for changes (brackets and underlining)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes relative to the patent being reexamined which are made to the specification, including the claims, must include the following markings: (1) The matter to be omitted must be enclosed in brackets; and (2) The matter to be added must be underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markings must follow paragraph (f) requirements so that insertions and deletions are clear in relation to the current patent text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of patent claims preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims may not be renumbered. The numbering of any claims added in the reexamination proceeding must follow the number of the highest numbered patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining claim numbering preserves continuity and is mandatory for amendments entered in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure amendment when required
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition, and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may order amendment of the disclosure to ensure internal consistency among claims, specification, and drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments relative to patent status date
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments must be made relative to the patent specification, including the claims, and drawings, which are in effect as of the date of filing the request for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are measured against the patent as it stood on the filing date of the reexamination request, not against subsequent changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on enlarging claim scope and introducing new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent or introduce new matter. No amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent. Moreover, no amendment, other than the cancellation of claims, will be incorporated into the patent by a certificate issued after the expiration of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are strictly limited to narrowing/clarifying the claims and cannot add new subject matter or broaden claim coverage; expired patents cannot receive substantive amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal effectiveness of amendments tied to reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Office actions will treat proposed amendments as though they have been entered, the proposed amendments will not be effective until the reexamination certificate is issued and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if amendments are entered for purposes of examination, they lack legal effect until issuance and publication of the reexamination certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry criteria for amendments in reexamination file
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments which comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d) through (j) (and are formally presented pursuant to 37 CFR 1.52(a) and 1.52(b), and contain all fees required by 37 CFR 1.20(c)) are entered in the reexamination file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure formal presentation, required markings, full-text presentation, and payment of required fees to have amendments entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PALM and IFW for reexamination file management
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Application Locating and Monitoring (PALM) system is used to support the reexamination process. The papers of a reexamination proceeding may be viewed on the Image File Wrapper (IFW). PALM provides information as to patent owner and requester, contents, status, and related Office proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent file is in paper form, it should be ordered and scanned into IFW for access throughout the prosecution. Reexamination status codes generally are in the “400” range (some in the “800” range for certain inter partes documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting events to PALM (which events to record)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PALM system is used to monitor major events during processing of reexamination proceedings. Examples to be reported include: Determination Mailed — Denial or Grant of request; Petition for reconsideration received; Decision on petition mailed — Denied or Granted; Owner response to determination received; Requester response to determination received; Mailing of all examiner actions; Receipt of owner’s responses and Office receipt date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each of these events (and any additional events reported by CRU Technical Support Staff) will be permanently recorded and displayed in the 'Contents' portion of PALM, with representative status displayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status and weekly PALM reports to assure special dispatch
rubrics_metrics.description: Various weekly reports are generated from PALM to assure reexaminations are processed with 'special dispatch.' Examples include: Preexam Reexam (requests not assigned by sixth week), Reexams Awaiting FA, Reexam Actions in CRU, Reexam PTAB (proceedings forwarded to PTAB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports are subdivided by working group and list requests in control number sequence to highlight approaching deadlines and must be acted on promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of reexamination to appropriate CRU art unit and examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination requests are generally assigned to the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) art unit which examines the technology in which the patent is currently classified. The CRU SPRS will assign the reexamination request to a primary examiner other than the examiner who originally examined the patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign to an examiner most familiar with the claimed subject matter; if no knowledgeable primary examiner is available in TC, assign to assistant examiner with primary examiner oversight/signature and conferring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner assignment policy — exclusion of original examiner unless necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the policy that the CRU SPRS will assign the reexamination request to an examiner different from the examiner(s) who examined the patent application. Exceptions include cases where the original examiner is the only examiner with adequate knowledge of the relevant technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assigned to the original examiner, CRU Director approval is required and must be stated in the decision on the request or indicated by the Director’s signature on the order or action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling copending reissue and reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reissue application is pending for a patent and a reexamination request is filed for the same patent, reexamination is generally assigned to a different examiner than the original patent examiner; if proceedings are merged, the merged proceeding will be handled by the examiner handling the reissue application, subject to exclusion rules if that examiner was involved in prior examination of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proceedings are not merged, decisions provide guidance on assignment depending on facts. If reexamination has been ordered or denied, specific procedures for timing, waiting on statements, notification to OPLA, and scanning of paper files into IFW apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and timeliness for objections to inadvertent assignment to original examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Should a reexamination be inadvertently assigned to an 'original examiner,' the party objecting must promptly file a paper alerting the Office within two months of the first Office action or other Office communication indicating the examiner assignment, or reassignment based on the objection will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reassignment will be addressed case-by-case. Assignment to original examiner by itself is not grounds for vacating Office decisions or 'restarting' the reexamination. When a party has no right of entry, the Office may waive rules to enter notification papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer procedure for reassignment to another art unit
rubrics_metrics.description: If the CRU SPRS to whose art unit the reexamination has been assigned believes the reexamination should be assigned to another art unit, consent of the CRU SPRS of the desired art unit should be obtained; any unresolved conflict is to be resolved by the CRU Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 35 U.S.C. 305, ex parte reexaminations must be conducted with special dispatch; transfers should be expeditious. If the new art unit accepts assignment, the new CRU SPRS assigns the request to an examiner in that unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time reporting for reexamination activities
rubrics_metrics.description: All USPTO personnel should report all time spent on reexamination on their individual Time and Attendance Reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even activities such as supervision, copying, typing, and docketing should be included to ensure accurate reporting of time expended on reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director‑initiated ex parte reexamination authority and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may determine at any time during the period of enforceability of a patent whether a substantial new question of patentability is raised by patents or printed publications discovered by the Director or brought to the Director’s attention, and may order ex parte reexamination without a request or fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director‑initiated reexamination is rare and used only in compelling circumstances after review of all facts. Authority delegated to Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy; decisions are mailed to patent owner. Requests from the public asking the Director to order reexamination are normally not considered; public should file a request under 37 CFR 1.510 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's decision timeline under 35 U.S.C. 303
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months following the filing of a request for reexamination under section 302, the Director will determine whether a substantial new question of patentability affecting any claim of the patent is raised by the request, with or without consideration of other patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A record of the Director’s determination will be placed in the official file and a copy mailed to the owner and requester. A determination that no substantial new question has been raised is final and nonappealable; partial refunds may be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner determination on ex parte requests (37 CFR 1.515)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months following the filing date of an ex parte reexamination request, an examiner will consider the request and determine whether a substantial new question of patentability affecting any claim of the patent is raised by the request and the prior art cited therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination is based on the claims in effect at the time, becomes part of the official file, and is mailed to the patent owner and requester. A patent owner statement and accompanying information submitted pursuant to §1.501(a)(2) will not be considered when making the determination. If no SNQ is found, a portion of the fee will be refunded. The requester may petition under §1.181 within one month of mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation search requirement before determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making a determination on the request for reexamination filed under 35 U.S.C. 302, a litigation search from Technical Support Staff (TSS) or STIC must be done to check if the patent has been, or is, involved in litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the 'Litigation Review' box on the jack et form (RXFILJKT) with search results and include a copy of the litigation search in the reexamination file history. If litigation is or was involved and a paper referring to court proceedings has been filed, reference that paper by number. If litigation is implicated, the matter should be promptly brought to the attention of the CRU SPRS to ensure conformity with Office litigation policy and guidelines (see MPEP §2286).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for granting reexamination — substantial new question of patentability (SNQ) and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: It is only necessary to establish that a substantial new question of patentability exists as to one of the patent claims in order to grant reexamination. The Office's determination in the order for reexamination and examination stage will generally be limited to a review of the claim(s) for which reexamination was requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 302 requires the request to set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested. If the requester fails to apply the art to certain claims, the requester is not statutorily entitled to reexamination of such claims; the Office may, at its discretion, reexamine non-requested claims or initiate reexamination of non-requested claims under 35 U.S.C. 303(a). No prima facie case of unpatentability need be found to grant an order for reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and limits of the decision on the request
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision on the request for reexamination should discuss all of the patent claims requested for reexamination. The examiner should limit the discussion to whether a substantial new question of patentability has been raised and SHOULD NOT reject claims in the order for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any rejection of claims will be made in the first Office action on patentability issued after the time for submitting any patent owner statement and requester reply. Patent owner claim scope statements submitted under 37 CFR 1.501(a)(2) will not be considered when deciding whether to order ex parte reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 304.
